title: Body Systems and Information Processing Review Test
description: Review practice connecting body systems, sensory pathways, evidence, models, and cells.

questions.prompt: Which level of organization is made of different tissues working together?
questions.questionText: Which level of organization is made of different tissues working together?
options: organ
cell
organism
molecule
questions.explanation: An organ is made of different tissues that work together for a function.

questions.prompt: Which statement best connects cells to tissues?
questions.questionText: Which statement best connects cells to tissues?
options: Similar cells can work together as a tissue.
Tissues are always nonliving.
A tissue is larger than an organ system.
Cells only exist in single-celled organisms.
questions.correctAnswer: Similar cells can work together as a tissue.
questions.explanation: Tissues are groups of similar cells working together.

questions.prompt: A student hears a timer and presses a button. Which structure detects the original stimulus?
questions.questionText: A student hears a timer and presses a button. Which structure detects the original stimulus?
options: sound receptors in the ear
food molecules in the stomach
red blood cells in the arm
bones in the finger
questions.explanation: The sound stimulus is detected by receptors in the ear before a response happens.

questions.prompt: Which body systems most directly work together to get oxygen from air to leg muscle cells?
questions.questionText: Which body systems most directly work together to get oxygen from air to leg muscle cells?
options: respiratory and circulatory
digestive and skeletal
nervous and digestive
skeletal and integumentary
questions.explanation: The respiratory system brings oxygen into the body, and the circulatory system transports it to cells.

questions.prompt: A model shows: food -> stomach and intestines -> nutrients in blood -> cells. What interaction does the model emphasize?
questions.questionText: A model shows: food -> stomach and intestines -> nutrients in blood -> cells. What interaction does the model emphasize?
options: digestive and circulatory systems moving materials to cells
nervous system storing only food memories
skeletal system digesting food
respiratory system making nutrients from bones
questions.correctAnswer: digestive and circulatory systems moving materials to cells
questions.explanation: The model shows digestion producing nutrients and blood transporting them to cells.

questions.prompt: A student claims, "The brain detects light before the eye does." Which correction is best?
questions.questionText: A student claims, "The brain detects light before the eye does." Which correction is best?
options: Light receptors in the eye detect light first, then signals travel to the brain.
The digestive system detects light first.
The eye responds after muscles move.
Light does not involve receptors.
questions.correctAnswer: Light receptors in the eye detect light first, then signals travel to the brain.
questions.explanation: Receptors detect stimuli before the brain processes the signal.

questions.prompt: A student studies outside on a cold day and starts shivering. Which explanation best connects stimulus and response?
questions.questionText: A student studies outside on a cold day and starts shivering. Which explanation best connects stimulus and response?
options: Temperature receptors detect cold, signals are processed, and muscles respond by shivering.
Bones detect cold and turn into muscles.
The stomach detects cold and stops all signals.
Shivering happens before the cold stimulus exists.
questions.correctAnswer: Temperature receptors detect cold, signals are processed, and muscles respond by shivering.
questions.explanation: This traces the pathway from environmental stimulus to receptor, signal processing, and response.

questions.prompt: Pulse data for one student: resting 72, after stairs 132, after five minutes 82. Which explanation best fits the pattern?
questions.questionText: Pulse data for one student: resting 72, after stairs 132, after five minutes 82. Which explanation best fits the pattern?
options: Activity increased circulatory demand, and rest allowed heart rate to move toward baseline.
The student's cells stopped needing oxygen after stairs.
The heart rate pattern is unrelated to exercise.
The skeletal system directly counted the pulse.
questions.correctAnswer: Activity increased circulatory demand, and rest allowed heart rate to move toward baseline.
questions.explanation: The pattern rises with activity and decreases after rest, supporting a claim about circulatory response.

questions.prompt: Which evidence would best support the claim that two body systems interact during digestion?
questions.questionText: Which evidence would best support the claim that two body systems interact during digestion?
options: Nutrients from the intestines enter the bloodstream and are carried to cells.
The stomach has a shape.
A person can name the digestive organs.
Food has different colors.
questions.correctAnswer: Nutrients from the intestines enter the bloodstream and are carried to cells.
questions.explanation: This evidence links the digestive system with the circulatory system.

questions.prompt: A diagram leaves out nerves between the brain and hand muscles. What is the most important weakness in the model?
questions.questionText: A diagram leaves out nerves between the brain and hand muscles. What is the most important weakness in the model?
options: It does not show how signals reach muscles for movement.
It shows too many cells.
It proves muscles do not need energy.
It explains digestion too well.
questions.correctAnswer: It does not show how signals reach muscles for movement.
questions.explanation: Without nerves, the model misses the signal pathway needed for coordinated movement.

questions.prompt: A person eats lunch and then bikes uphill. Which explanation best connects digestion, circulation, respiration, and muscles?
questions.questionText: A person eats lunch and then bikes uphill. Which explanation best connects digestion, circulation, respiration, and muscles?
options: Food molecules and oxygen are supplied to muscle cells, where energy is released for work.
The stomach directly pushes the pedals.
The lungs digest the lunch before oxygen enters.
Muscles work without cells or materials.
questions.correctAnswer: Food molecules and oxygen are supplied to muscle cells, where energy is released for work.
questions.explanation: This connects multiple systems to cellular energy release during exercise.

questions.prompt: A student says, "A reflex means no nervous system is involved because it happens quickly." Which response is best?
questions.questionText: A student says, "A reflex means no nervous system is involved because it happens quickly." Which response is best?
options: Reflexes are quick because nervous-system pathways can process some responses rapidly.
Reflexes are controlled only by the digestive system.
Reflexes prove receptors are not needed.
Reflexes happen before any stimulus.
questions.correctAnswer: Reflexes are quick because nervous-system pathways can process some responses rapidly.
questions.explanation: A quick response can still depend on receptors and nervous-system signal pathways.

questions.prompt: Which investigation would best test how exercise affects the circulatory system?
questions.questionText: Which investigation would best test how exercise affects the circulatory system?
options: Measure pulse before exercise, immediately after exercise, and after rest.
Look at a drawing of a bone once.
Ask which food tastes best.
Count how many windows are in the classroom.
questions.correctAnswer: Measure pulse before exercise, immediately after exercise, and after rest.
questions.explanation: Pulse is evidence about circulatory activity, and comparing times can show the effect of exercise.

questions.prompt: Which example best transfers the body-systems idea to a new situation?
questions.questionText: Which example best transfers the body-systems idea to a new situation?
options: A bird flying uses muscles, bones, oxygen intake, circulation, and nerve coordination.
A feather has one color pattern.
A bird has a beak.
A nest can be made of twigs.
questions.correctAnswer: A bird flying uses muscles, bones, oxygen intake, circulation, and nerve coordination.
questions.explanation: The same systems-interaction idea can be applied beyond humans to other animals.

questions.prompt: Which explanation best connects this concept back to cells?
questions.questionText: Which explanation best connects this concept back to cells?
options: Body systems support the needs of cells, and specialized cells help the systems do their jobs.
Cells are unrelated to organs.
Only organs are living, not cells.
Organ systems replace the need for cells.
questions.correctAnswer: Body systems support the needs of cells, and specialized cells help the systems do their jobs.
questions.explanation: This connects the previous cells concept with the body-systems concept: cells make up systems and systems help cells meet their needs.
